rooms.title: Bar & Games Room — Evening Speakeasy
rooms.description: The Bar & Games Room spans the full 100-foot width of the house and 45 feet of its depth, about 4,500 sq ft. In standing mode roughly 3,500 sq ft is available to guests, with room for about 250 comfortably or about 350 packed. The default setup combines the intimacy of a speakeasy with a private London club and a hint of 1920s Paris. The fully equipped, stocked east-wall bar has a solid Kentucky limestone counter, oxblood frontage, copper pendants and six spaced bottle-green stools. Albury Acoustics custom-built the room’s sound system. Staff can play CDs, vinyl or streaming audio through the behind-the-bar playback system, which also has an AUX input. Seven small round café tables with 18 oxblood chairs and a 13 ft oxblood banquette on the south wall opposite the stage bring everyday seating to about 29. The west games end has a full-size 9 ft billiards table, a 16 ft shuffleboard table at the south end, two Bally pinball machines and a restored 1956 Wurlitzer 2000 Centennial jukebox. The pinball machines are Creature from the Black Lagoon (1992) and Theatre of Magic (1995), with the KAWS sculpture nearby. In speakeasy mode guests use the Wurlitzer’s original selector buttons to play 45 rpm singles. Albury Acoustics adapted its audio output to feed the room’s custom sound system. Bottle-green panelling and herringbone timber frame the room. The lit back bar and table lamps provide the everyday light. The permanent raised stage at the north end is 36 by 16 ft and takes a full band, a string quartet or a DJ booth. The dark mahogany Welmar pub upright and its stool sit at floor level beside the east wing. It came from The Freemasons Arms, Long Acre, Covent Garden, where it had stood since the early 1960s before the pub’s corporate refurbishment. The provenance is fictional. For live music, light the stage and bring in the instruments for the chosen setup. For nightclub mode, move the café tables and chairs to the perimeter, keeping the central dance floor and routes clear. The fixed stage, six-stool bar, oxblood banquette and floor-level Welmar stay in place. A temporary black oak DJ booth sits at centre stage, with two world-class professional DJ decks, a mixer and a pair of Albury A-Series cue monitors. A retractable projection screen is centred behind the booth. A PA speaker and compact subwoofer flank the booth on each side as part of the custom-built Albury Acoustics sound system. There is working space behind the booth and a clear route to the backstage door. In nightclub mode the DJ controls the room sound and jukebox playback is disabled. House lights are off. Discreetly integrated ceiling fixtures wash the dance floor in blue and violet and cast a warm spot on the decks. The table lamps glow at the perimeter, and KAWS stays on its plinth. Guest double doors open from the stair and lift lobby on the south. The guest corridor also serves the cinema, tasting room, listening lounge and washroom suite, with four enclosed WCs and a shared vanity plus a separately accessed accessible WC. The north-wall stage door leads to the 10 by 12 ft Backstage Store / Preparation Room, with a second door to the service corridor from the mews. A separate door at the rear of the bartender aisle connects the bar to the service kitchen and pantry between it and the same service corridor. Two framed original 1970s concert posters hang to the left of the stage, one of them Bowie. A framed 1950s press photograph of a pianist at the keys hangs above the Welmar. The framed pieces stay up in nightclub mode.

rooms.title: Backstage Store / Preparation Room
rooms.description: The north-wall door behind the permanent stage leads to the Backstage Store / Preparation Room, approximately 10 by 12 ft (3.05 by 3.66 m). It is allocated directly north of the bar within the existing under-garden upper-basement envelope, behind the full-width main bar. Dark walnut cupboards on the west wall hold instruments, cases, cables, small amplifiers and folding stands; a five-foot oxblood bench sits on the east wall below a large brass-framed mirror with two vertical brass-and-opal sconces giving even face light. A soft opal ceiling light illuminates the centre aisle and bench, with concealed task lighting inside the instrument cupboards. The warm-white lighting is dimmable and has high colour rendering, with an indicative 3000 K / CRI 90+ specification for preparation use. Coat hooks and a shallow rear shelf serve performers, with the middle aisle kept clear. The stage door opens from a fixed rear landing at stage level. A second door opens to the mews service corridor. This is local support for bar performances, separate from Music Nobile’s main technical/instrument store. It is not the storage destination for billiards, shuffleboard or the Welmar piano. The stage, landing and back room remain in place in everyday, live-music and nightclub configurations. Room dimensions and door geometry are approximate design-reference allocations, not surveyed construction dimensions.

rooms.title: Principal Kitchen & Breakfast Room
rooms.description: Approximately 900 square feet, Albury’s daily production kitchen is a room-scale professional residential workspace rather than a domestic kitchen enlarged with expensive appliances. The 24-foot working wing has a 22-foot cooking-and-appliance wall and one 15-by-5-foot stool-free island, with visibly clear five-foot aisles on every side. The island provides separated mise-en-place stations, refrigerated drawers, shallow tool storage, a narrow dry-goods pull-out, prep sink, integrated waste and power; the rear wall carries a 180 cm range and full-width extraction, while tall green joinery conceals combi-steam and conventional ovens, warming drawers, full-height refrigeration and freezer storage. The garden-facing breakfast table occupies its own bay six feet beyond the island.

rooms.description: Approximately 900 square feet, Albury’s daily production kitchen is a room-scale professional residential workspace rather than a domestic kitchen enlarged with expensive appliances. The 24-foot working wing has a 22-foot cooking-and-appliance wall and one 15-by-5-foot stool-free island, with visibly clear five-foot aisles on every side. The island provides separated mise-en-place stations, refrigerated drawers, shallow tool storage, a narrow dry-goods pull-out, prep sink, integrated waste and power; the rear wall carries a 180 cm range and full-width extraction, while tall green joinery conceals combi-steam and conventional ovens, warming drawers, full-height refrigeration and freezer storage. rooms.title: Studio Albury — Live Room
rooms.description: The full-width, approximately 100-by-30-foot live room occupies the garden side of Music Nobile. Its east half occupies No. 32’s double-height former ballroom and its west half has a normal-height ceiling. Two enclosed normal-height isolation booths sit within the room, one for three to four voices and one for a seated string quartet. The live room and control room are built as acoustically isolated floating rooms. Independent inner glazing sits behind the heritage garden windows, and separate glazing assemblies divide the live and control rooms. For concerts, recording equipment goes to the technical store and portable risers from the same store form a temporary stage along the garden windows. The control room and the separate rec room are on the street side of the first floor.

rooms.description: An illustrative future landscape proposal for No. 34, not the August 2025 opening condition. The acquired house is empty, separate and unused; planning is expected to take about two years before works. A future staff house, kitchen garden, event lawn and controlled garden connection remain proposed facilities.

rooms.title: Existing Site — Before Landscape Works
rooms.description: The illustrative pre-works aerial shows Albury and detached No. 34 as separate plots before the new staff-house enclosure, kitchen garden, hedge arch and unified rear landscape are formed.

rooms.title: Street Arrival
rooms.description: From just inside the open gates, the broad approach, balanced frontage and single formal entrance establish Albury as one residence rather than two adjoining houses.

rooms.title: Front Elevation
rooms.description: The unified Upper Phillimore frontage reads as one exceptionally broad Victorian residence while retaining the measured rhythm of the original Nos. 30 and 32 pair.

rooms.title: Front Elevation at Blue Hour
rooms.description: Restrained window light and the entrance lanterns give the restored public frontage an inhabited evening presence without turning it into an event façade.

rooms.title: Duchess of Bedford Walk Mews
rooms.description: The screened rear service frontage contains the secure vehicle ramp, controlled personnel entrance and secondary service access without exposing the garden or principal rooms. The upper-basement garage and loading court sit under the terrace and lawn. Vehicles enter down the screened Duchess of Bedford Walk mews ramp beyond the garden’s north wall. The service route joins the garage and loading, event kitchen and backstage.

rooms.title: Garden Overview
rooms.description: From the unified elevation, the 100-by-131-foot rear garden resolves into a 30-foot terrace, 68-by-65-foot open lawn, sixteen-foot side gardens and a deep planted far room. The 68-by-65-foot lawn holds about 300 standing in good weather or 100 in the seated marquee layout.

rooms.title: Rear Terrace
rooms.description: The 100-by-30-foot full-width pale limestone terrace has a permanent bronze-framed canopy, side screens and heaters. The east end has a bar. The everyday layout seats fourteen for dining and twelve in the lounge, with a clear central route. It holds about 200 standing with the canopy closed.

rooms.title: Looking Back to the House
rooms.description: From the far-lawn threshold, the 65-foot lawn and broad unified elevation read at their full scale; the fixed Hepworth remains halfway down the west border. The 68-by-65-foot lawn holds about 300 standing in good weather or 100 in the seated marquee layout.

rooms.title: Far-Garden Salon
rooms.description: The fixed ten-seat north-west salon sits beneath retained canopy and looks south across the full lawn; no sculpture occupies this room.

rooms.title: Former No. 34 Boundary — Existing Condition
rooms.description: The stock-brick wall, hedge, eight pleached limes and bronze-and-timber bench record the east boundary before the acquired grounds are opened into Albury through the new hedge arch and landscape works.

rooms.title: Garden at Blue Hour
rooms.description: Residential step wash, shielded border lights, restrained tree uplight and one sculpture light preserve the same fixed geometry after sunset. The 68-by-65-foot lawn holds about 300 standing in good weather or 100 in the seated marquee layout.

rooms.title: Marquee Dinner Configuration
rooms.description: A single ballasted 48-by-52-foot clear-span marquee centres one hundred dinner places on the lawn, retaining ten-foot side clearances, seven feet from the terrace and six feet before the far garden. The 68-by-65-foot lawn holds about 300 standing in good weather or 100 in the seated marquee layout.
